title: Finite-presentation section calculus on the qcqs pro-etale site
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $V\to X$ be an object of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site] with $V$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. For every small filtered diagram of abelian sheaves $(F_i)$ on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], the canonical map $\varinjlim_i F_i(V)\to(\varinjlim_i F_i)(V)$ is bijective. Let $A$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and let $P$ be an $A$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which is pro-etale locally the cokernel of $A^m\to A^n$, with $m,n$ finite nonnegative integers. For every small filtered diagram of $A$-module sheaves $(N_i)$ the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,N_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,\varinjlim_iN_i)$ is bijective. The maps are induced by the given colimit coprojections; thus equality of two representatives holds at a common later stage. Colimits are sheaf colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: Work throughout in $\mathcal C=V_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Every covering of a qcqs object $T$ has a finite affine refinement: choose a finite affine open cover of $T$, and over each open use the finite list of affine source opens in the definition of a pro-etale covering. Their union is finite, still covers, and refines the original covering. The opens and composites are arrows of the site by its definition. For two members $U_a,U_b$, the map $U_a\to T$ is qcqs by qcqs morphism permanence (1); base change (3) and composition with the qcqs scheme $U_b$ in (2) show that $U_a\times_TU_b$ is qcqs. Its fibre product exists in the site by the qcqs-site-limits node. Thus every qcqs $T$ has finite affine covering refinements with qcqs overlaps; no intersection is assumed affine.

proof.text: For a small filtered diagram of abelian groups $B_i$, use the set of pairs $(i,b)$ modulo $(i,b)\sim(j,c)$ when there are arrows $i\to k\leftarrow j$ giving equal images. Filteredness makes this transitive: take a common target of two equality witnesses and equalize the two arrows from their shared middle index. Define addition by sending two representatives to a common stage and adding there; further common targets and equalization show independence of the choices. Zero and negatives are represented by zero and negatives at a stage. Every compatible cocone induces exactly one homomorphism on these classes, so this is the abelian-group colimit by the colimit universal property. The same construction with scalar multiplication is the colimit of modules over a fixed ring. Consequently every element has a stage representative, equality is witnessed by arrows to a common stage, and any finite collection of representatives and equality witnesses can be moved to one stage. The last assertion follows by repeatedly taking common targets and equalizing the finitely many parallel arrows; it does not require the filtered category to be a poset.

proof.text: Let $(F_i)$ be the abelian-sheaf diagram and put $F=\varinjlim_iF_i$. Its colimit is the sheafification of the presheaf $Q(T)=\varinjlim_iF_i(T)$ by the site-abelian-colimits node. The underlying set sheafification agrees with abelian sheafification by the underlying-sets node. Thus the local-sections node applies: sections of $F$ are locally images of elements of $Q$, and two elements of $Q(T)$ with the same image are equal after a covering of $T$. By step 2 these local elements lift to actual stage sections and these local equalities are eventual equalities. All these assertions use the supplied coprojections: the identification of the sheafification with $F$ is the unique isomorphism respecting them. Enlarge the working set universe, as allowed by the size convention, to contain the site and diagram data; this satisfies the local-sections node's universe hypothesis. Abelian sheaves satisfy the cited module-sheaf sheaf axiom by their canonical integer action $n x=x+\cdots+x$ (and negatives), so steps 4 and 5 may use that definition for them.

proof.text: For any qcqs object $T$, suppose $s\in F_i(T)$ and $s'\in F_j(T)$ have the same image in $F(T)$. By step 3 they become equal in $Q$ on a covering. Refine it to the finite affine covering of step 1. On each member step 2 supplies arrows to a stage where the restricted sections agree. Choose a common target and equalize the finitely many arrows from $i$ and $j$ so that there is one chosen arrow from each of these indices. At that stage the two sections agree on the finite covering and hence on $T$ by the sheaf separation axiom. This proves injectivity of $\varinjlim_iF_i(T)\to F(T)$, including its eventual-equality form.

For $t\in F(T)$ with $T$ qcqs, step 3 and then step 1 give a finite affine cover $(U_a\to T)$ and stage sections $s_a$ representing $t|_{U_a}$. Move them to one stage $i$ by step 2. Their restrictions to each qcqs overlap $W_{ab}=U_a\times_TU_b$ have equal images in $F(W_{ab})$; step 4 supplies eventual equality there. For the finitely many overlaps, take a common target of the witnesses and equalize the finitely many arrows from $i$. The transported sections now agree on every overlap, so the sheaf axiom glues them to a section at that stage over $T$. Its image is $t$ by separation. If the cover is empty, $T$ is empty and both groups of sections are zero; choose any index, which exists by filteredness. This proves section bijectivity for every qcqs object of $\mathcal C$, and in particular for $T=V$.

Now fix the ring sheaf $A$ and the module diagram $(N_i)$ with colimit $N$. Forgetting to abelian sheaves preserves the colimit by the module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful node, so steps 4 and 5 give $\varinjlim_iN_i(T)\cong N(T)$ for every qcqs $T$, compatibly with $A(T)$-actions. Refine a presentation covering for $P$ by step 1 to a finite affine cover $(U_a\to V)$, with $A^{m_a}\xrightarrow{r_a}A^{n_a}\xrightarrow{b_a}P\to0$ on $\mathcal C/U_a$. Presentations remain presentations after further slice restriction: underlying abelian restriction is exact by the site-restriction-exact node, and the module forgetful functor computes kernels and cokernels. In particular it reflects exactness, since zero underlying kernel or cokernel is the zero module sheaf. Finite free sheaves restrict to finite free sheaves by their sectionwise description. This checks the presentations on every qcqs $W\to U_a$, including the overlaps.

proof.text:
On $\mathcal C/U_a$ write $r_a(e_\ell)=\sum_{k=1}^{n_a}a_{k\ell}e_k$, with $a_{k\ell}\in A(U_a)$. For each qcqs $W\to U_a$ and any module sheaf $M$, a map $A|_W\to M|_W$ is uniquely determined by the image of $1$ in $M(W)$: on an object $Z\to W$ it sends $f$ to $f$ times the restriction of that image. Consequently the cokernel universal property gives the natural identification
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A|_W}(P|_W,M|_W)=\ker\left(M(W)^{n_a}\longrightarrow M(W)^{m_a}\right),\qquad (x_k)\longmapsto\left(\sum_k a_{k\ell}|_W x_k\right)_\ell.$$
No surjectivity of $A(W)^{n_a}\to P(W)$ is being asserted: the universal property is in sheaves. Apply filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits to this finite-product and kernel diagram of abelian groups. Step 6 identifies the colimits of the $N_i(W)$ with $N(W)$, and the matrix maps correspond because the coprojections are $A$-linear. Therefore $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{A|_W}(P|_W,N_i|_W)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A|_W}(P|_W,N|_W)$ is bijective for every such $W$. Its two representative assertions are exactly those of step 2. Ranks $m_a=0$ or $n_a=0$ use empty products, so are included.

proof.text: Given $h:P\to N$, step 7 with $W=U_a$ lifts every $h|_{U_a}$ to a morphism $h_a:P|_{U_a}\to N_i|_{U_a}$ at one common stage after transporting finitely many lifts. On each qcqs $W_{ab}$, the two restricted morphisms have equal images in $\operatorname{Hom}(P|_{W_{ab}},N|_{W_{ab}})$. Use step 7 with the presentation restricted from $U_a$ to witness equality at a later stage. Step 2 makes all the finitely many witnesses hold with one arrow from $i$. Since the sheaf Hom of the defining node is a sheaf, the resulting morphisms glue to $g:P\to N_j$. Its image equals $h$ on the cover and hence globally. Conversely, if two global morphisms at stages $i,i'$ have equal images, step 7 on each $U_a$ witnesses their equality at a later stage; step 2 makes one pair of arrows $i\to j\leftarrow i'$ work for the whole finite cover. Sheaf Hom separation then gives equality globally. This proves both surjectivity and injectivity of the canonical Hom map and the claimed common-stage equality. On the empty scheme, sheaf Hom has its unique empty-cover section, so the same conclusion holds. Every comparison just used is postcomposition with the supplied coprojections, as the formula in step 7 and gluing show.
